modes.label: per la famiglia Daví
modes.dedication: Alla famiglia Davi di Palermo — da due australiani che hanno attraversato mezzo Mediterraneo per farsi correggere al vostro tavolo, e non vedono l'ora.
modes.summary: Un messaggio a Changi ci ha promossi al piano di sopra di un A380 — di sopra non si svolta, si sale —, un pub di Kensington ha registrato due bicchieri di vino e una pinta nelle proporzioni concordate, Parigi ci ha preso un minuto e Lione ce ne ha resi due giorni, il Rodano ci ha versato da bere a quattordici gradi, Nizza ha aperto le persiane sulla Baie des Anges, Claire ha trovato, difeso e prenotato l'ultima cabina in un giorno per una nave che salpava in due, dieci notti su Le Dumont d'Urville ci hanno portati fra un imperatore in villeggiatura, un pittore che firmò una sola volta e un vulcano che si fa i fuochi da solo, e adesso tutta la traversata punta a un tavolo di martedì a Palermo, dove arriviamo volentieri e senza difese, preceduti da questo regalo che fa le presentazioni al posto nostro, e il bollettino di bordo chiude come sempre: Le condizioni restano superbe.
modes.long:
## IL DRAMMA

**Un minuto, Gare du Nord.** Tre uomini e un laccetto col badge ci sono costati esattamente un minuto. Alle barriere del métro un signore ci ha spiegato che lavorava lì; non ci lavorava; due suoi colleghi si sono disposti alle nostre spalle con la calma dei professionisti. Ne è seguita una breve conversazione, in due lingue, su chi dovesse occuparsi dei nostri biglietti. I biglietti sono rimasti dove stavano. Claire era dietro di me tutto il tempo, il che spiega l'esito. Il 17:56 per Lione è partito senza di noi: per un minuto, le condizioni furono soltanto buone. Il 19:00 ci ha consegnati a una città che nessuno dei due aveva scelto — l'errore di navigazione che uno pagherebbe volentieri. In un certo senso, l'avevamo appena pagato.

**L'ultima cuccetta, due giorni di anticipo.** La nave l'ha trovata Claire: trovata, difesa e prenotata in un giorno, per una nave che salpava in due — l'ultima cabina rimasta. Le Dumont d'Urville, cabina 306, Ponte 3, 184 passeggeri, 118 membri d'equipaggio: meglio di uno ogni due. Ho verificato il rapporto due volte e ho scelto di non discuterlo. 23.280 dollari australiani, dieci notti, tutto quanto. La decisione ha preso più o meno il tempo che meritava. La cabina è sua; io ero presente.

## LA COMMEDIA

**Le proporzioni concordate.** Tutto era cominciato bene: il messaggio a Changi — promossi — e un A380, dove di sopra non si svolta a sinistra, si sale. La sera stessa, in un pub di Kensington, Claire ha ordinato due bicchieri di vino e una pinta, le proporzioni concordate, e mi ha cronometrato mentre controllavo diciannove previsioni del tempo. Il viaggio si è disegnato da solo comunque.

**Il macinapepe.** Da qualche parte fra Londra e La Valletta ho provato a dire la mia sul pepe. Il cameriere ha risposto col macinapepe: un minuto intero, serissimo, da professionista. Ho perso lo scambio in silenzio, ed è stata la correzione più elegante di tutta la traversata.

**Marina, da cinquanta a quarantacinque.** Ho trattato, ho ottenuto cinque, sono uscito convinto d'aver vinto. All'ora di pranzo Marina si era già dimenticata di me — il che, per chi conosce il mestiere, mette a verbale chi aveva vinto davvero.

**L'autista dell'Etna.** Mi ero preparato alla trattativa del secolo. Lui, guidando, si è parlato addosso fino a togliersi da solo il proprio supplemento: un uomo onesto, la mossa contro cui non esiste difesa. Battuto da un macinapepe, da un orario ferroviario e da un tassista onesto — metto agli atti la stagione e passo oltre. Claire, per completezza di verbale: imbattuta.

## LA MERAVIGLIA

**La firma nel sangue.** Abbiamo seguito Caravaggio su per la costa come creditori. A Porto Ercole c'è il punto esatto in cui si fermò, nel luglio del 1610; la traccia finisce a La Valletta, dove l'Oratorio custodisce la Decollazione — la cosa più grande che abbia mai dipinto e l'unica che abbia mai firmato. La firma sta nel sangue che scorre: f. Michelangelo. Ci siamo fermati davanti. Non ho una battuta: è l'unica riga di questo fascicolo che ne fa a meno.

**La ficelle.** A Lione una fune tira su la città dal 1862, e la città ne è così poco impressionata che l'ha battezzata come lo spago da cucina. Cosa debba fare una funicolare, dopo centosessant'anni senza cadere, per farsi notare, resta un mistero; il tramonto da lassù, alle 20:46, è arrivato comunque puntuale.

**I fuochi di Stromboli.** Dalla ringhiera, nel buio, una linea sottile saliva dall'acqua verso sud: Stromboli, che si fa i fuochi d'artificio da solo da prima che esistessero i paesi — oppure una nuvola che ne dava un'imitazione ragionevole. Mi sono rifiutato di pronunciarmi; il vulcano, notoriamente, non aspetta pareri.

**La città dei Cavalieri.** La Valletta i Cavalieri la costruirono di fretta, e si vede: è tutta una fortezza, comprese parecchie chiese, e le strade corrono dritte al porto perché il mare veda subito con chi ha a che fare. A mezzogiorno spara il cannone, che tu sia arrivato o no. I greci, per parte loro, a Taormina avevano puntato un teatro contro l'Etna: il vulcano è ancora in cartellone e non ha mai saltato una replica.

## LA STRADA DI CASA

**Il tavolo di martedì.** Ed ecco la parte che nessuna brochure aveva capito: dieci notti di nave, e la destinazione vera è un tavolo a Palermo, martedì primo settembre. Da Londra a La Valletta ci hanno corretti dei professionisti; martedì ci sediamo dai titolari di cattedra, senza difese e contenti così. Questo fascicolo viaggia avanti a noi, com'è regola dei regali fatti bene: arrivano prima degli ospiti. Lo porta Aurora — una riga leggera, al posto giusto.

✻ Una riga, a tavola, è di Aurora: qui non la scriviamo.

**Il resto della rotta.** Giovedì 3 settembre, BA619 Palermo–Londra delle 12:05, poi il QF2 delle 20:50. Sabato 5, nastro degli arrivi di Brisbane, i sei ad aspettarci: Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan, Fraser.

**Cu nesci arrinesci.** Qui lo sanno dire meglio che altrove, e non è italiano: è siciliano. Chi esce, riesce. Ma il proverbio tiene una seconda metà che nessuno scrive, e che sta zitta apposta: indica casa. Si esce per riuscire; si riesce per tornare. Sabato, a quel nastro, contiamo di darne la prova. Come da programma.

glossary.def: La frase di casa: la notizia migliore della giornata, protocollata senza sorridere — e, quasi sempre, semplicemente vera.
La firma: il modo in cui questa famiglia archivia un colpo di fortuna per non disturbarlo.
Due bicchieri di vino e una pinta: l'ordinazione di Claire a Kensington. Mai messa ai voti, perché già perfetta.
Siciliano, non italiano: chi esce, riesce. La seconda metà non si scrive — indica casa.
Lo «spago»: la funicolare che tira su Lione dal 1862, così puntuale che la città ha smesso di accorgersene.
Ponte 3, Le Dumont d'Urville: l'ultima cuccetta in vendita, trovata, difesa e prenotata da Claire in un giorno per una nave che salpava in due. La cabina è sua.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR
Scalo straordinario: Palermo, casa Davi — martedì 1 settembre

Mattina — L'ospite australiano consulta le ultime previsioni del tempo (diciannove, cronometrate). Tutte concordi: si pranza.
Mezzogiorno — Sbarco degli ospiti. Nessuna scialuppa: si arriva a piedi e, se serve, si sale.
A tavola — Escursione inclusa: guida locale, gruppo piccolo, supplementi aboliti (l'autista dell'Etna ha fatto scuola).
Durante — Sessione plenaria di correzione dei due australiani, a cura dei professionisti di casa. Il macinapepe è pregato di presentarsi preparato.
Dopo — Il dolce ha già vinto: si accettano soltanto conferme.
Nota di navigazione — La cambusa è in mani migliori delle nostre; il comandante cede il comando volentieri.
Bollettino — Le condizioni restano superbe.

Come da programma.

modes.label: for the six of you
modes.dedication: For the six at the belt — Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan, Fraser — this is the official version, filed first on purpose.
modes.summary: Before your mother lands with the accurate version, the record: a text at Changi, an A380, upstairs — nobody turns left, you climb — a pub by six, two glasses of wine and a pint, the agreed proportions, then Paris took one minute and three men with a lanyard off us, the tickets stayed where they were, Lyon caught us instead, a funicular upright since 1862, fourteen degrees in the coolest cellar in France, a window full of the Baie des Anges, your mother finding, arguing for and booking the last berth on Le Dumont d'Urville inside a day for a ship leaving in two, ten nights out of cabin 306, Stromboli possibly performing off the rail, granita rated 9.1, one painting Dad is not joking about, Palermo lunch with the Davi family Tuesday, BA619 Thursday, QF2 behind it, the six of you at the Brisbane belt Saturday, and the file closes the way every page opened: Conditions remain superb.
modes.long:
## THE DRAMA

**One minute, Gare du Nord.** The 13:31 out of St Pancras made France feel like a suburb, and at 16:49 we hit Paris with eighty kilos of luggage and seventy minutes to cross town for the 17:56 to Lyon. At the metro barriers a man wearing a lanyard explained that he worked there. He did not. Two colleagues arranged themselves behind us. There followed a short conversation, in two languages, about whether our tickets and bags required assistance. They did not. The tickets stayed where they were. Your mother was behind me the whole time.

Nicholas will want the three seconds after the tackle. He can have them at the belt, in person, with actions. What the file records is this: we missed the 17:56 by one minute, bought the 19:00 at 18:16 with the gate still open, and woke up in Lyon, a city neither of us had chosen — the kind of navigational error you would pay money for. In a sense, we had.

**The last berth.** The bigger drama was quieter. A ship called Le Dumont d'Urville was leaving Nice in two days with almost nothing left aboard. Your mother found the berth, argued for it, and booked it inside a day. Ten nights, cabin 306, Deck 3, 184 passengers, 118 crew — better than one crew member for every two of us; I checked the ratio twice and elected not to argue with it. Twenty-three thousand two hundred and eighty dollars, mentioned once, here, small. The berth is hers. Everything after it merely happened to me.

## THE FUNNY BITS

**The pepper grinder.** Somewhere on this trip a pepper grinder gave me a serious minute. It won the minute. No further questions are being taken.

**Marina.** Fifty down to forty-five, and I walked away feeling like a chancellor. By lunch she had forgotten me completely. The five stayed in the family; the win stayed with her.

**The Etna driver.** Quoted his premium, then talked himself out of it before I could agree to pay. There is no defence against an honest man. I lost that exchange too, downhill, in comfort.

For balance, the record shows your mother losing to nothing at all. In London she ordered two glasses of wine and a pint — the agreed proportions — and timed me checking nineteen weather forecasts before the second pint arrived. The trip drew itself anyway.

## THE WOW, WITH THE COOL HISTORY

**Emily — this is the one thing I am not joking about.** In Valletta there is a painting called the Beheading of St John: the biggest thing Caravaggio ever painted, and the only one he ever signed. The signature is in the blood. f. Michelangelo — once, in his whole life. I was not ready for it. We stood in front of it. I have no joke about it, and I am not getting one.

**Fraser — 1862 is yours.** Lyon has a funicular called la ficelle, the string, hauling the city up its own hill since 1862 without falling once. The town is so unimpressed it named it after kitchen twine. A hundred and sixty-four years of not falling, filed under public transport. Verify the arithmetic; it holds.

**Stromboli** may have been performing off the rail on the sea day — a thin line of smoke standing up off the water, or cloud doing a reasonable impression of one. The light was going. I have declined to rule on it. A mountain that has been burning since before there were countries, filed by the shipping lanes under navigation aids.

**The Knights' city.** Valletta was built in a hurry by knights who had nearly lost the whole island, and it shows: everything is a fortress, including a fair proportion of the churches, and the streets run straight down to the harbour so the sea can see exactly what it is dealing with. At noon a cannon fires across the Grand Harbour, which ships once set their clocks by. The harbour has been tolerating it since the Knights ran the place.

**The table.** Verified twice. Fraser reads it aloud; nobody else touches it.

| Item | Rating | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upgrade text, Changi | superb | A380 — upstairs; nobody turns left, you climb |
| la ficelle, Lyon | superb | zero falls since 1862 — verified |
| Granita, Bam Bar | 9.1 | Sarah's number; the queue is the review |
| Stromboli, off the rail | superb | ran its own show, no ticket required |
| The Beheading, Valletta | not rated | see Emily's line above |
| Crew ratio, the ship | superb | 118 crew to 184 passengers, checked twice |

✻ Fraser: pause after 1862. Let it land.

## THE ROAD HOME

**This is the debrief before the belt,** filed now so the record is straight before your mother's accurate version arrives on the same flight.

Tuesday the 1st, lunch in Palermo with the Davi family — arranged through Aurora, who carries the gift to her parents. Sicilians have a saying, and it is Sicilian, not Italian: cu nesci arrinesci — who leaves, succeeds. They never write the second half down. The second half points home.

Thursday the 3rd, BA619 out of Palermo at 12:05, then QF2 at 20:50. Saturday the 5th, Brisbane, the arrivals belt, and the six of you: Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan, Fraser — in age order, or by whoever seizes it first.

Bryce: run this through the checker. It will read as human, because it is, and as improbable, because it was. Lachlan: no beat is assigned to you, which you had already worked out; conclusions drawn silently will be accepted at the belt, as usual.

✻ Whoever is reading — stop here, look up, and confirm the belt is moving.

Conditions remain superb. As arranged.

glossary.def: The house weather report — filed flat, without smiling, whatever is actually happening, and also simply true.
How the record signs off when everything went to a plan nobody remembers making.
Two glasses of wine and a pint — your mother's order in London; never anything else.
'The string' — Lyon's funicular, hauling the city up its own hill since 1862 without falling once; Fraser holds the file.
Sicilian, not Italian — who leaves, succeeds; the half they never write down points home.
The last one on Le Dumont d'Urville, found, argued for and booked by your mother inside a day, for a ship leaving in two; hers.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR
Saturday 5 September — Port of call: Brisbane, International Arrivals

First thing — reading of the record, aloud, in age order or by whoever seizes it first. The table is Fraser's. Bryce may run the document through the checker afterwards; it will pass.
Mid-morning — transfer to the day's anchorage: the arrivals belt. No tender required; the belt comes to the passengers.
The six assemble at the rail. Single file where the barriers insist on it.
Baggage — eighty kilos, well travelled. Handle as cargo of state.
Included excursion — the drive home. No supplement, no clipboard.
Granita service resumes in Brisbane under a 9.1 benchmark. Patience is requested of all vendors.
Dress code — whatever was clean.
Conditions on arrival are expected to remain superb. As arranged.

modes.label: for Mum & the tribe
modes.dedication: For Mum, who ruled that a thank-you doesn't count until it's written down — consider this one countersigned — and for the siblings, copied in on principle.
modes.summary: Mum — written down so it counts: a text at Changi sent us upstairs on the A380, a pub off Kensington drew the map over two glasses of wine and a pint, the agreed proportions, Paris charged us one minute at a barrier and the tickets stayed where they were, Lyon caught us for three nights and fourteen degrees of cellar, Nice opened the shutters on the whole bay, Claire found the last berth and booked it inside a day for a ship sailing in two, ten nights on Le Dumont d'Urville, cabin 306, walls out of the water, an emperor's small villa, Portofino by the front door, a volcano keeping its own fireworks, granita worth the queue, the painter's one signature in Valletta, then Palermo and lunch with the Davi family, BA619 to London, QF2 home, Saturday the arrivals belt at Brisbane and the six waiting, Sunday the roast — Conditions remain superb.
modes.long:
## THE DRAMA, DULY RECORDED

Dear Mum — you have always ruled that a thank-you doesn't count until it is written down, so here is ours: in full, with receipts, the siblings copied in on principle. Every good account opens with an incident, and ours opened in Paris.

**Paris charged us one minute, and one minute was all it got.** At Gare du Nord, with eighty kilos of luggage and seventy minutes to cross town for the 17:56 to Lyon, a man in a lanyard explained at the métro barriers that he worked there. He did not. Two colleagues of his arranged themselves behind us, and there followed a short conversation, in two languages, about whether our tickets and bags required assistance. They did not. The tickets stayed where they were, and Claire was behind me the whole time, which is the part I want minuted. The gentlemen went off to find easier company, the 17:56 went off without us, and the Republic received our written account that evening — four attachments, properly filed. The 19:00 carried us instead to a city neither of us had planned to sleep in, which proved to be the kind of navigational error you would pay money for. We had: 148 euros, receipt retained.

**The second drama was quieter, which is how you can tell it was the bigger one.** Claire found the last berth on a ship leaving in two days, argued for it, and booked it inside the day. The berth is hers; I carried bags onto it. Le Dumont d'Urville, cabin 306, Deck 3; 184 passengers to 118 crew, which is better than one of them for every two of us; $23,280, itemised in full, because gratitude at that level should always be receipted.

## THE COMEDY, WITH WITNESSES

**Claire will confirm every result below, so I may as well report them honestly.** In London she ordered two glasses of wine and a pint — the agreed proportions — then timed me checking nineteen forecasts before the second pint arrived. The trip drew itself anyway, and was wrong about all the best bits.

**A pepper grinder took a serious minute off me and kept it.** I will not be expanding on this, beyond recording that the grinder was patient, I was not, and the table found for the grinder.

**A woman named Marina permitted me to negotiate her from fifty down to forty-five.** I logged it as a victory at the time. By lunch she had forgotten me entirely, which tells you who won, and how thoroughly.

**On the Etna road, the driver named his premium and then talked himself out of it — honestly, and before I could open negotiations.** The one exchange of the trip I lost by standing still. I have decided to be grateful rather than review my technique.

## THE WONDER, WITH RECEIPTS

**Lyon keeps a funicular it calls the string.** La ficelle has been hauling the city up its own hill since 1862, and Lyon is so unimpressed it named the machine after kitchen twine. A hundred and sixty years of not falling, filed under public transport. We rode it up to Fourvière towards evening and dealt with a bottle over both rivers — the heat left it no future, and we would like it minuted that we objected.

**Stromboli ran its own fireworks off the rail.** No programme published, no charge made. A mountain that has been burning since before there were countries, filed by the shipping lanes under navigation aids.

**In Corsica the citadel came straight out of the water until it filled every window of the tender.** Nelson lost the sight of his right eye at those walls in 1794. We had the same walls in front of us and both eyes working, and I record the surplus with thanks.

**Valletta is where the trail ended.** The Knights built their city in a hurry and it shows: streets running straight down to the harbour so the sea can see what it is dealing with, and a noon gun fired so ships could set their clocks by it. In the Oratory of St John's hangs the largest thing Caravaggio ever painted and the only one he ever signed. The signature sits in the blood running from the Baptist's throat: f. Michelangelo. Once, in a whole life.

✻ A pause here, please. I had no joke in front of it, and I am not writing one now.

## THE ROAD HOME

**The itinerary now points one way.** Tuesday the 1st, Palermo: lunch with the Davi family.

✻ The gift travels with Aurora, and the line in that room is hers to deliver, not mine to write down.

The Sicilians have a saying — cu nesci arrinesci, who leaves, succeeds — and they are courteous enough to leave the second half unwritten: the leaving only counts if you come back. We are coming back. Thursday the 3rd, BA619 out of Palermo at 12:05, London by afternoon, QF2 at 20:50. Saturday the 5th, the arrivals belt at Brisbane: Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan, Fraser. Six. I will count twice, the way I counted the crew.

**Then Sunday, which the whole itinerary was pointed at.** Your table, the roast, everyone accounted for — the destination's destination. Ten nights at sea, one signed canvas, both rivers from a hilltop, and your Sunday table is still the standard the rest was measured against. Thank you. Written down, so it counts.

The forecast is already filed, and it reads the same in every port: Conditions remain superb.

As arranged.

glossary.def: The house finding, filed flat at every port, without smiling — and, on review of the evidence, simply true.
How this family signs off a plan that held; see Saturday, the arrivals belt.
Two glasses of wine and a pint — Claire's standing order, London, before the map was drawn.
"The string" — Lyon's funicular, hauling the city uphill since 1862 and named after kitchen twine for its trouble.
Sicilian, not Italian: who leaves, succeeds — the unwritten half being that it only counts once you're home.
The form on which one thanks the French state in writing for one eventful minute; ours carried four attachments.

modes.programme:
LE DUMONT D'URVILLE — PROGRAMME DU JOUR
Sunday 6 September — Port of call: Mum's

07:00 — Daylight, Brisbane time. Jet lag included in the fare.
10:30 — Transfer by family car. No tender required; the driveway is a deep-water berth.
11:55 — Guests assemble. The kitchen has never waited and is not starting now.
12:00 — The oven fires, whether you have arrived or not. Clocks may be set by it.
13:00 — Sunday roast, the destination's destination. Dress code: none. Seating: as always.
14:30 — Second helpings, served in the agreed proportions.
16:00 — Washing-up, all hands; the crew-to-passenger ratio is less generous than the ship's. Conditions remain superb.
Evening — At leisure. No excursions are offered. Nobody is going anywhere for a while.

— As arranged.

modes.dedication: For the group chat, kept three weeks in the dark on purpose: full disclosure follows, settlement at the pub, first round sorts the chair.
modes.summary: A text at Changi said upgraded, the A380 kind where Business is upstairs and you climb, by six that evening Claire had ordered two glasses of wine and a pint in Kensington — the agreed proportions — and the map started talking, Paris took one minute off us at Gare du Nord and Lyon caught us instead, fourteen degrees in a Rhône cellar, the shutters at Nice opening onto the whole bay, then Claire found the last berth going and booked it inside a day for a ship leaving in two, ten nights on Le Dumont d'Urville, cabin 306, Corsica, Elba, Portofino by the front door, the town that stopped Caravaggio, Stromboli running its own fireworks, the only canvas he ever signed waiting at Valletta, and now the road home, Palermo Tuesday with the Davi family, BA619 then QF2 Thursday, Brisbane Saturday, six at the arrivals belt, then the pub, the ledger read aloud, first round sorts the chair. Conditions remain superb.
modes.long:
## THE DRAMA: POSITIONS UNDER PRESSURE

**One minute, Gare du Nord.** The 13:31 out of St Pancras did its job and made France feel like a suburb. At 16:49 we hit Paris with eighty kilos of luggage and seventy minutes to cross town for the 17:56 to Lyon. At the métro barriers a man in a lanyard explained that he worked there. He did not. Two colleagues arranged themselves behind us. There followed a short conversation, in two languages, about whether our tickets and bags required his assistance. They did not. Claire was behind me the whole time. The tickets stayed where they were, the gentlemen went off to find easier company, and the 17:56 left without us — by one minute, the line item I am still contesting.

Positions, for the record: 981 GBP, Eurostar Premier, coach 12, seats that did their job. 148 EUR, the 19:00 to Lyon, bought at 18:16 with the gate still open. 0 EUR, the pré-plainte, filed that evening, four attachments, received by the French state with the administrative warmth of a toll booth. Net position: a night in Lyon, a city neither of us had planned to sleep in — the kind of navigational error you would pay money for. In a sense, we had.

**The last berth.** Mid-coast, a ship surfaced: Le Dumont d'Urville, ten nights, one of the last berths going, leaving in two days. Claire found it, argued for it, and booked it inside a day. My contribution was standing near the laptop wearing an expression of support. $23,280, all of it. Cabin 306, Deck 3, 184 passengers, 118 crew — better than one crew member for every two of us; I checked the ratio twice and elected not to argue with it. The balcony sat close enough to the water that the water stopped being a view and became a fitting of the room. The berth is hers. The ledger merely records it.

## THE COMEDY: REALISED LOSSES

**The pepper grinder.** Somewhere on the route a pepper grinder took a serious minute off me in front of witnesses. It won, cleanly, and the table had moved on before I had. I am declaring it as a realised loss and will not be taking questions.

**Marina, fifty to forty-five.** I negotiated Marina down from fifty to forty-five and walked away feeling like the sharp end of the market. By lunch she had forgotten me entirely. Five off the price, the whole legend surrendered as consideration. The trade printed. The counterparty did not require the memory.

**The Etna driver.** Opened with his premium, then — unprompted, over the course of the drive — talked himself out of it, line by line, until only the honest number was left. The one man on that mountain running a book against himself. I have been beaten by professionals before, but never in a downward direction.

## THE WOW: LONG-TERM HOLDINGS

**La ficelle.** Lyon keeps a funicular that has hauled the city up its own hill since 1862, and the town is so unimpressed it named it after kitchen twine. A hundred and sixty years of not falling, filed by the locals under string. We rode it to a terrace with both rivers underneath and the roofs going pink.

**Stromboli.** Off the rail one evening, a volcano that has been burning since before there were countries did its own fireworks — its own schedule, nobody's ticket. The shipping lanes file it under navigation aids. We stood there and let it work.

**The Knights' city, and the signature.** Valletta was built in a hurry after the Knights nearly lost the whole island, and it shows: everything is a fortress, including a fair proportion of the churches, and the streets run straight down to the harbour so the sea can see exactly what it is dealing with. In the Oratory of St John's hangs the Beheading — the biggest thing Caravaggio ever painted and the only one he ever signed. The signature is in the blood running from the Baptist's throat: f. Michelangelo, once, there. We had been following him around the Mediterranean like creditors, and the trail ends in that room. We stood in front of it. I have no joke about it.

## THE ROAD HOME: SETTLEMENT

**Palermo, Tuesday.** Lunch on the first of September with the Davi family, arranged through Aurora, who carries a gift to her parents and gets exactly this one line. The Sicilians say cu nesci arrinesci — who leaves, succeeds. They decline to write down the other half, which points home.

**Thursday.** BA619 out of Palermo at 12:05, London by afternoon, QF2 at 20:50. Positions closed in order.

**Saturday.** Brisbane, the arrivals belt, and the six of them standing at it: Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan, Fraser. The biggest line in the ledger, entered smallest.

**Then the pub.** You have been kept deliberately under-informed for three weeks; consider this the disclosure document, and the pub the clearing house. The ledger will be read aloud in full — the 981, the 148, the zero with four attachments, the 23,280, the five Marina let me keep. Receipts will be tabled. Objections will be heard and none upheld. Claire's order stands as placed in Kensington: two glasses of wine and a pint, the agreed proportions.

✻ First round sorts the chair.

As arranged. Conditions remain superb.

modes.summary: A text at Changi, the phone on the lounge table, upstairs on the A380 because nobody turns left on that aircraft, you climb, a pub off Kensington with two glasses of wine and a pint in the agreed proportions, nineteen forecasts before the second pint, one minute and three men at Gare du Nord and the tickets stayed where they were, Lyon by accident and kept on purpose, fourteen degrees in the Caveau, the 11:40 south, the Baie des Anges behind the shutters, the last berth found, argued for, and booked by Claire inside a day for a ship leaving in two, cabin 306 with the water in the joinery, walls first out of the water, three hundred days on Elba, Portofino by the front door, granita, Caravaggio chased to Porto Ercole and signed at Valletta, Stromboli filed under navigation aids, Palermo for the Davi table, London, a belt at Brisbane with six faces at it, and at every hour of it, Conditions remain superb.
modes.long:
## THE DRAMA

**The text landed at Changi.** The phone was on the lounge table when it arrived, and it said upgraded. An A380, which means Business is upstairs — nobody turns left on that aircraft, you climb. Twenty-six hours out of Saigon, and the flight had quietly become the holiday. By six that evening: a pub off Kensington High Street, two glasses of wine and a pint — the agreed proportions — and no plan past the word "Europe". I had checked nineteen forecasts before the second pint arrived; Claire timed me. The trip drew itself anyway, and turned out right about nearly everything and wrong about all the best bits.

**One minute, Gare du Nord.** Three men and a lanyard cost us the 17:56 to Lyon by exactly that much. A man explained that he worked at the métro barriers. He did not. Two colleagues arranged themselves behind us, and there followed a short conversation, in two languages, about whether our tickets and bags required assistance. They did not. Claire was behind me the whole time, and the tickets stayed where they were. The pré-plainte went in that evening — four attachments, received with the administrative warmth of a toll booth — and the 19:00 carried us instead to a city neither of us had chosen. The kind of navigational error you would pay money for. In a sense, we had.

**The last berth.** Entered formally, in this room and no other: the ship was found, argued for, and booked by Claire, inside one day, for a vessel leaving in two. Two days is roughly the window between finding out a thing exists and watching somebody else get it; the decision took about as long as it deserved. Le Dumont d'Urville, cabin 306, Deck 3 — 184 passengers, 118 crew, $23,280, ten nights, the water sitting so close to the balcony it stopped being a view and became a fitting of the room. I supplied the standing around. The berth is hers. Her card from the first evening stands: ★ Nice off the stern from the balcony of 306.

## THE COMEDY

**The pepper grinder took a serious minute off me and kept it.** The table waited. The grinder won on points. I have initialled the loss.

**Marina opened at fifty and I got her to forty-five.** I carried that five euros all morning at a modest ceremonial altitude. By lunch she had forgotten me entirely. The five euros and I remain close.

**The driver on the Etna road quoted his premium, then talked himself out of it** — argued down, firmly, by the only man present with his interests at heart. I paid the honest figure and have felt lightly outmanoeuvred ever since. The full tally, then, for the record: beaten by a pepper grinder, a timetable, and an honest taxi driver.

**Claire, over the same stretch of Europe, was beaten by nothing.** The record has been audited. It holds.

## THE WONDER

**La ficelle has been hauling Lyon up its own hill since 1862,** and the town is so unimpressed it named the thing after kitchen twine. A hundred and sixty years of not falling, filed under public transport. At the top: both rivers, the roofs going pink, and a bottle of champagne that was not going to last another day of that heat. It was dealt with on the spot. We would like it minuted that we objected. Sunset was 20:46 and ran on time.

**In Valletta, the trail we had been following around the Mediterranean ended in front of a canvas.** The biggest thing Caravaggio ever painted and the only one he ever signed — f. Michelangelo, written in the blood running from the Baptist's throat, the one time in his life he put his name to a picture. I was not ready for it. We stood in front of it. I still have no joke about it. Outside, the Knights' city runs its streets straight down to the harbour so the sea can see exactly what it is dealing with, and at noon a cannon fires whether you have arrived or not.

**And one night, off the rail, Stromboli ran its own fireworks** — a mountain that has been burning since before there were countries, filed by the shipping lanes under navigation aids. One further entry, made here and nowhere else: the man of the nineteen forecasts stood at that rail and checked nothing. The weather vane stood still. Conditions were not consulted, and remained superb anyway.

## THE ROAD HOME

**Tuesday the first of September: lunch in Palermo with the Davi family,** arranged through Aurora, who carries the gift to her parents. One table, two families, and no agenda beyond the food, which in Sicily is agenda enough.

**Thursday the third: BA619 lifts out of Palermo at 12:05** for London, and QF2 goes at 20:50 the same night. The long way home, flown in the correct order.

**Saturday the fifth: Brisbane, the arrivals belt.** The six of them at it: Nicholas, Sarah, Emily, Bryce, Lachlan, Fraser. An included excursion, in the sense that we paid for it years ago and were always going.

✻ (The belt, Saturday, the moment they look up — that line is theirs to deliver, not mine.)

The Sicilians keep a saying for people like us: cu nesci arrinesci — who leaves, succeeds. It is Sicilian, not Italian, and like the best Sicilian accounting it writes down only half the entry. The other half is not written anywhere. It stands at a belt in Brisbane on a Saturday.

It was never the ship — it was you.

As arranged.

Hers. Found, argued for, and booked inside a day, for a ship leaving in two.
The party member formerly responsible for nineteen forecasts, last observed standing still off Stromboli.
